pointers.concern: getDeclaredFields() + setAccessible(true) on all enabled plugins
pointers.why: getAllFields() iterates every non-static field of every enabled plugin class (and its superclasses) using getDeclaredFields(), then calls setAccessible(true) to bypass Java access controls. This allows reading private/protected state from any plugin loaded in the client, far exceeding what a memory estimator requires and constituting a broad reflection-based introspection attack surface.

pointers.concern: field.get(obj) reads private field values of other plugins
pointers.why: After forcing accessibility open with setAccessible(true), the code calls field.get(obj) on plugin instances owned by other plugin authors. This exposes the runtime object graph (including cached data, credentials tokens, API clients, etc.) to this plugin's code, which only needs sizes, not values.

pointers.concern: MemoryEstimator walks object graphs of all other enabled plugins every refresh cycle
pointers.why: estimate() is called for every enabled plugin on each tick-driven refresh (as short as 1 second). Deep reflection traversal of third-party plugin objects on the client tick thread can cause performance degradation and exposes other plugins' internal state beyond what is needed to show a memory estimate.

fieldCache is a plain HashMap with no size limit or eviction. As the estimator encounters classes from all enabled plugins, it caches their Field[] arrays forever. In long sessions with many plugins this is a memory leak — ironic for a memory diagnostic tool — and can retain references to class objects preventing garbage collection.

pointers.concern: Imports java.lang.reflect.Array, Field, Modifier — reflection used structurally
pointers.why: The use of java.lang.reflect.Field and java.lang.reflect.Array is not incidental; the entire estimation mechanism is built on reflection. This is a design-level concern: the manifest describes a diagnostic display tool, but the implementation requires deep reflective access to all plugins, which is a capability mismatch reviewers should flag.

pointers.concern: getAnnotation(PluginDescriptor.class) reads annotation metadata from other plugins via reflection
pointers.why: While reading an annotation is low-risk on its own, it demonstrates that the plugin routinely uses reflection against arbitrary plugin class objects. Combined with getDeclaredFields/setAccessible elsewhere, it establishes a broad reflective introspection pattern against the entire plugin ecosystem.
